title: Speculative prefetch / speculative-exec deduplication in metering pipeline
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Problem summary: The inference runtime performs speculative prefetches and speculative decoding in a small percentage of requests to reduce tail latency. Those speculative paths can produce token fragments that are later discarded by the public response (e.g., a different beam or fallback path chosen). The metering pipeline currently credits all emitted tokens without distinguishing speculative vs final output. This leads to overcharging for some workloads and inconsistent customer invoices, especially for streaming clients that reconnect or for requests that trigger model switching or fallbacks. Scope: This ticket covers detection, tagging, and de-duplication of speculative-prefetched token events in the online metering pipeline (not the offline billing batch job changes).
impact: Customer-visible overbilling (medium-high) for inference patterns that use speculative execution or prefetch. Internal cost leakage for high-throughput customers using dynamic routing. Metric noise in token-per-request dashboards and broken SLOs for per-request latency vs cost analyses.
proposed_solution: 1) Ingress tag: add a stable request-level header that marks tokens emitted from speculative paths (speculative=true) and includes a request fingerprint. 2) Metering pipeline change: add a short-lived dedupe layer keyed by (request_fingerprint, token_position, token_hash) with time-window semantics (default 30s) to suppress double-crediting of speculative fragments that are later superseded. 3) Attribution: if a token is later chosen as final, ensure attribution persists to the same request_fingerprint and is counted once. 4) Fallback handling: when automatic model fallback emits tokens and the original model also emitted speculative tokens, the dedupe layer should credit only the chosen variant with a fallback-tag resolution step. 5) Metrics & audit: emit explicit counters for suppressed-speculative-tokens, dedupe-evictions, and ambiguous-attributions to help investigations. Implementation notes: use existing in-memory LRU store in meter-worker for short windows; fall back to Redis for cross-worker dedupe for Dedicated clusters. Bloom filter alone is insufficient because we need deterministic attribution; prefer bounded LRU with token hashes.
tradeoffs:
- Strict dedupe can undercharge if speculative markers are lost (client/library upgrades). We mitigate by conservative default window and audit logs that surface high suppression rates.
- Cross-worker dedupe adds Redis dependency and a small latency penalty; we make it optional per deployment (on for Dedicated, off for single-node hosted).
- Token hashing and position-based keys assume stable tokenization across model variants; for heterogeneous model switching, require canonical tokenizer mapping upstream.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Integration test harness that simulates speculative prefetch, fallback, and reconnect scenarios shows no double-counted tokens in 1000 fuzzed cases. 2) UNIT tests for dedupe window behavior and eviction. 3) Deployed on staging with telemetry showing suppressed-speculative-tokens > 0 for synthetic workload and no increase in total billed tokens for control traffic. 4) Reconciler job shows <0.1% variance with offline billing for staged dataset after change.
implementation_steps: Add speculative header and request_fingerprint propagation in runtime (PR: github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/4128)
Extend meter-worker to compute token_hash and perform LRU dedupe (PR: github.com/redwood/metering/pull/79)
Feature flag gating and Redis integration for cross-worker dedupe (PR: github.com/redwood/metering/pull/80)
End-to-end tests and fuzz harness for streaming reconnect + speculative flows (tests in repo: github.com/redwood/tests/tree/spec-dedupe)
Staging rollouts: canary -> region-wide -> global with monitoring alerts
rollout_plan: Phase 1: feature-flagged rollout in staging (1 week) with synthetic loads. Phase 2: enable for 10% hosted traffic and Dedicated test clusters (2 weeks). Phase 3: enable by default for Dedicated and provide opt-in for Hosted; monitor for invoices anomalies for 30 days. Emergency rollback flag to disable dedupe and revert to old metering behavior.
monitoring_and_alerts: Add dashboard tiles: suppressed_speculative_tokens/sec, dedupe_evictions/sec, dedupe_miss_rate, billing_delta_24h. Add alerts if suppressed_speculative_tokens spikes > 10x baseline or if billing_delta_24h > 0.5% for major tenants.
testing_plan: - Unit tests for token_hash correctness and window TTL. - Integration test that replays traced requests with speculative fragments and validates final billed tokens equal expected. - Chaos test: drop speculative header mid-request to validate conservative fallback. - Load test: ensure dedupe store memory bounded under 10k keys per worker for typical loads.
open_questions: 1) Should speculative markers originate in runtime or be inferred by inference router? 2) For multi-hop streaming (interleaved fragments), do we need position-less dedupe? 3) How to handle long-lived clients that pause > TTL and then resume (risk of double-charge)?
